stem: The elements in Group 17 are known as the halogens.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem: Between the molecules of Group 17 elements van der Waals' forces exist.
parts.text: State the trend in the relative strength of van der Waals' forces down Group 17.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: State the physical state of each of the halogens under room conditions.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
A solution of aqueous bromide ions, $\text{Br}^-\text{(aq)}$, is added to separate samples of $\text{Cl}_2\text{(aq)}$ and $\text{I}_2\text{(aq)}$.

Describe what is observed in each reaction. Explain your answer in terms of the relative reactivity of these elements as oxidising agents.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Bleach is made by reacting $\text{Cl}_2$ with cold $\text{NaOH(aq)}$.

Write an equation for the reaction of $\text{Cl}_2$ with cold $\text{NaOH}$.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem: When $\text{ClO}^-\text{(aq)}$ is added to water, it behaves as a Brønsted-Lowry base.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Write an ionic equation for the reaction between $\text{ClO}^-$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
The concentration of $\text{NaClO}$ in bleach **S** is $x\text{ g dm}^{-3}$.

$\text{NaClO}$ reacts with $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2\text{(aq)}$ as shown.

$$\text{H}_2\text{O}_2\text{(aq)} + \text{NaClO(aq)} \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O(l)} + \text{NaCl(aq)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)}$$

A $5.00\text{ cm}^3$ sample of **S** completely reacts with $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2\text{(aq)}$. The volume of $\text{O}_2\text{(g)}$ produced is $24.0\text{ cm}^3$ under room conditions.

Assume that only the $\text{NaClO}$ in **S** reacts with $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2\text{(aq)}$.

Calculate $x$. Show your working.

parts.label: (f)
parts.text:
Sodium chlorate(I), $\text{NaClO}$, oxidises dilute hydrochloric acid to form three products. The products which contain chlorine have chlorine species with oxidation number $-1$ or $0$.

No other species changes its oxidation number during the reaction.

Use this information to complete the ionic equation.

$$\ldots\ldots\text{ClO}^- + \ldots\ldots\text{HCl} \rightarrow \ldots\ldots + \ldots\ldots + \ldots\ldots$$
